q: Then he’s going through all these scenarios like how do you break down the Doona if baby is sleeping? What if I’m grocery shopping? Do I push the stroller and the grocery carriage together? Who does the grocery shopping in your sisters house? It looks big and bulky ect.
cx: At 28 weeks her husband questions the Doona car-seat stroller her family bought off the registry.

q: He asks if we can buy one around here in person then looks up the car seat to then say that it’s expensive and we’ll just have to grab it from his moms.
cx: The gifted seat was shipped to his mother's house hours away; he wants one now in case of early labour.

q: At that next appointment, blood was taken, and we were told we’d be contacted if anything was wrong. We never received a call.
cx: A husband says a test was never run until 14 weeks; they paid privately to check.

q: I am on maternity leave but my husband (24M) is still working due to him getting a new job last year and he will be reaching a year with his company in August and thats when he'll start his leave. Since he is still working during the night I do everything myself so he can rest
cx: A month after the birth; her husband can't take leave until a year in his new job.

q: I did give birth sooner than expected and we had nothing prepared (baby was born at 35 weeks).
cx: Why the first weeks caught them unprepared.

q: My mom asked us to move in with her so she can help us out. The only thing is that she works the night shift so I am still on my own until she gets home.

q: My mom asked me why I’m so tired all the time and this isn’t normal I should see a doctor. She’s not happy about me being tired at all basically saying it’s my fault.
cx: At 15 weeks with her second, working full time with a 3-year-old.

q: I wake up daily at 5:30am to get ready for my day. I work full time in an office 5 days a week from 8am-4pm. Before I get to work I do the drop offs at daycare for my son so my morning starts off crazy.

q: I asked dad to hold the dogs and he said "sure, over you get 'Fatty'!" I couldn't believe my ears.. did he just call me 'fatty??' he was laughing as he said it.

q: i work 40 hour weeks and come home exhausted. my partner doesn’t help me at all. […] i feel like im constantly begging for help that i don’t receive. i don’t know what to do to keep my house in order when i am at this level of exhaustion.
cx: At 12 weeks she broke down because no room in the house is livable.

q: our bills are 60/40 where I pay majority because I pay the health insurance and everything for the pregnancy this far and I'm expected to do all the cooking cleaning and groceries shopping or it never gets done. I've planned everything for the baby too.
cx: Venting about a husband who leaves all money, housework and baby planning to her.

q: Meanwhile I've gained 40lbs from pregnancy and he makes me feel like a tub of lard telling me to workout after birth!!!

q: We men have absolutely 0 idea how women feel and it can be a bit overwhelming feeling powerless to help or understand.
cx: Long-distance boyfriend whose partner at 8 weeks has gone quiet.

q: I read online that it can be exhausting to even say “I love you” over message. Is that actually true? I don’t remember the last time she said it.
cx: Checking online reading about early-pregnancy fatigue against strangers.

q: We’re 16 days post partum and my in laws are all visiting. […] They have been needing to be entertained this entire visit and keep asking “so what are we doing next?”
cx: Crying in her bedroom while three in-laws stay over.

q: MIL will not put my baby down even when I insist he needs to sleep. So he didn’t sleep all morning and has been having a rough day.

q: My mom came the week after baby was born and did our laundry and cooked and cleaned for us. I just can’t get over how selfish these people are.

q: To be honest, she has been doing a lot of the heavy lifting for things up to now with regards to our baby. She's been doing all of the research, booking us in for baby sessions etc. I've really only driven her there and tried to make sure I am there to support her but I've not led any of the baby prep at all.
cx: UK husband, wife at 25 weeks, realises she carries all the preparation.

q: Her mum is planning to come and live with us for a few months after she gives birth. I know that's not a fix and will come with its own set of problems, but yeah, it's something.
